newsitem.title: USA: UPS calls Teamsters strike irresponsible.
newsitem.headline: UPS calls Teamsters strike irresponsible.

text.p: The United Parcel Service termed a strike called by the Teamsters union on Sunday "irresponsible" and vowed to give priority to emergency packages after the strike begins at midnight EDT (0400 GMT).

"We are extremely disappointed that the Teamsters have chosen to walk out on these informal settlement talks," UPS chief UPS negotiator Dave Murray told reporters shortly after Teamsters representatives left the negotiations.

Murray said the company would give priority to hospital packages, perishables, and blood supplies. "We will do what we can with those packages that have to get where they're going ... Those are the ones we would try to dig out and get to the people who need them," he said.
Murray said that UPS believed that international operations would not be affected, because they were run by a separate unit of the company.

Murray called on the union to put the UPS offer to its members for a vote. "We believe what they should be doing instead of setting up picket lines, they should be out sending that final offer out for a ratification vote. Let the people decide," he said.
"We think it's highly irresponsible of them to talk about strikes at this time, which will endanger the well-being of 300,000 UPS employees and their families," Murray said.
